batch_strategy: Select all 32 rows simultaneously, retaining the supplied premeasurement predictions unchanged. Combine missing ratio-by-amount experiments around recent failures, controlled loading-setup comparisons, and tests of unsupported response-curve shapes. Include one repeat-condition catalog row to assess a consequential loading anomaly.

choices.reason: m174 at 50/1, 100 ul locates the completion rise preceding the recently measured 100/1 values. Rows 2424b103c34d3d2b6a9a and 36b45fbdbace5950c108 finished at 63.30 and 61.66 mL, with substantial acquisition-time underprediction. This missing ratio segment tests whether the current approximately 30 mL completion forecast captures the amount-dependent curve.

m174 at 50/1, 150 ul completes the selected amount contrast. Measured low-loading row b0764b94416833704b53 finished at 32.42 mL, while all measured 100/1 amounts finished much later. The pair distinguishes a largely ratio-driven rise from an additional completion association with amount at 50/1.

m38 at 10/1, 100 ul interpolates between measured low- and high-loading completions of 30.74 and 38.39 mL in 86fb9a8fd6633397d670 and d1e922c04dbd0c9f6c06. The latest high-loading completion was underpredicted at acquisition. This label tests the updated interpolation and, with selected 5/1, constrains the middle-loading solvent slope.

m35 at 10/1, 50 ul starts a controlled amount pair below the measured 20/1 contrast. Rows dc419b3ce4e1382aae7a and e97ed592e525b9c30dec differ substantially in onset but little in completion. This label helps locate how early that endpoint-specific amount association develops.

m35 at 10/1, 150 ul completes the pair. The current forecasts already allow earlier onset at higher amount; measurement tests its magnitude and whether completion remains comparatively stable. Together with measured 20/1 and 50/1 endpoints, the pair teaches ratio-dependent loading response for an aromatic ketone.

m205 at 1/1, 150 ul tests amount transfer from b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8, which measured 10.51/25.36 mL at 50 ul. Its completion exceeded the acquisition forecast. Comparison with selected m206 at the same sample volume tests whether the observed setup difference persists beyond low loading.

m206 at 1/1, 150 ul complements measured low-loading row fe69b1dbb4d976f830cd and the selected m205 condition. Their low-loading completions already differ by about 9.25 mL. These labels assess amount-dependent transfer of that difference while retaining their different DCM loading volumes and densities.

m206 at 2/1, 50 ul joins its measured low-loading 1/1 and 5/1 conditions. Existing middle-loading row 13bfaf03c35b4cff3bd5 anchors 2/1. This tests both the location of its solvent-response rise and the onset association with amount in the region where m205 behaves quite differently.

m208 at 5/1, 50 ul fills the low-loading segment before measured 10/1 row e9e7a737df389d5fcc13 and the larger 20/1 rise. The completed 10/1 amount series supports onset movement with comparatively stable completion. This label constrains solvent curvature before assuming that weak-solvent loading behavior applies throughout the curve.

m168 at 10/1, 150 ul in 400 ul DCM has an existing 300 ul counterpart, 037298044b4fc8868e5e. The latest 2/1 high-amount volume contrast again associated 400 ul with earlier completion. One additional label tests transfer across ratio and amount without spending another full pair.

m88 in neat EA, 150 ul sample and 400 ul DCM supplies a loading-volume comparison with measured 200 ul DCM row 5024a0270c82cc68fd48. That row finished at 12.76 mL. This tests whether loading-volume information transfers to an amino ester and helps establish boundaries on the m168 association.

m127 at 2/1, 50 ul forecasts approximately 11.61/23.72 mL, above measured 5/1 row c40d715383d042030e93 at 6.36/15.33 mL. A local maximum in stronger solvent is unverified. This starts an amount contrast that can distinguish an actual recorded response from transfer of an inappropriate curve.

m127 at 2/1, 100 ul completes the selected amount contrast in the forecast peak region. Both 2/1 forecasts have completion near 24 mL, while measured 5/1 loading endpoints finish earlier. The labels test the peak across amount and constrain a sparsely measured strong-solvent segment.

m81 at 5/1, 100 ul begins a fixed-amount solvent comparison. At 150 ul, 5879dc8ccb560446d54c finished at 20.27 mL at 5/1, whereas 7d402b3fad455f06fe68 finished at 9.74 mL at 10/1. Measuring the middle amount tests whether this unusual completion decrease extends across loading.

m81 at 10/1, 100 ul completes the solvent pair and adds an amount comparison between measured 10/1 endpoints ce11189a0e59d1798306 and 7d402b3fad455f06fe68. It tests whether the current intermediate completion is appropriate and whether the 5/1-to-10/1 decrease depends strongly on amount.

m75 at 20/1, 100 ul tests the predicted completion decrease from the measured 5/1 middle-loading value in f82f2844c7e27afd32bb. The numerous remaining rows for this diester make its condition-response mapping relevant to the Row-distribution. The forecast dip remains unmeasured and should be tested locally.

m75 at 50/1, 150 ul adds a high-loading counterpart to low-loading row 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e. Its completion forecast is nearly unchanged despite a threefold amount difference, and its single-predictor completion quantiles are broad. The label tests that invariance alongside the selected intermediate-ratio point.

m190 in neat EA, 100 ul forecasts later onset and completion than measured 1/1 row 03e8372f11ac433be4fa. This unverified strong-solvent peak is a useful transfer test among phenolic aldehydes, where m197 and m186 have distinct observed endpoint patterns.

m190 at 2/1, 100 ul brackets measured 1/1 with the selected neat-EA condition. Its onset forecast falls below the measured 1/1 onset before rising again at selected 5/1. The resulting fixed-loading segment tests the predicted response shape rather than inferring it from OH count or bulk polarity.

m190 at 5/1, 100 ul extends the selected strong-solvent segment toward measured 50/1 row 7d9c7f40bc71ee7c4ef0. Comparison with selected m186 at the same sample volume probes positional bromine environment and recorded loading setup jointly; their different amounts and DCM volumes prevent a purely structural attribution.

m186 at 5/1, 100 ul forecasts an onset hump between measured 2/1 row 43758e84c67aabf44a9f and 10/1 row 79faae5899539a97f8d9, whose onsets are both near 4.6 mL. This tests a specific interpolation shape and supplies a local comparison for m190 without transferring m197's extended completion indiscriminately.

m197 at 10/1, 50 ul fills the fixed-loading gap between measured 5/1 row a91850e587e062097c02 and 20/1 row f6b05afc9acf85dffb0f. After ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3 rejected the neat-EA middle-amount completion trough, locating the weaker-solvent rise is more informative than revisiting that interpolation.

m197 at 10/1, 150 ul completes the amount pair. The forecasts allow earlier onset at higher amount but very similar completion. Existing high-loading 2/1 and 50/1 labels provide wider anchors, so the new pair tests endpoint-specific amount transfer within the missing solvent segment.

m19 in neat EA, 100 ul supplies the strong-solvent endpoint of a selected fixed-amount comparison. Measured high-loading row 309a91add8b07c02e65b anchors this ratio, while the latest 1/1 low-loading result showed substantial onset movement. This extends loading-response learning to a tertiary-amine acrylate.

m19 at 1/1, 100 ul fills the amount gap between a595d5f1882c39914392 and 97297c71a28a2ccbdeeb, whose onsets differ by 4.80 mL while completion is similar. Together with selected neat EA, it tests both the updated amount interpolation and the solvent response at fixed loading.

m33 at 5/1, 100 ul starts an amount pair in the missing segment between 1/1 and 10/1. The latest 10/1 pair and completed neat-EA series support completion associations with amount, while the measured 1/1 endpoints have the opposite direction. This label helps locate the change in response.

m33 at 5/1, 150 ul completes the pair. Current completion forecasts are nearly flat between 100 and 150 ul. Comparison with measured high-loading 1/1 row 22191f76e895327c6e2d and 10/1 row ba4d64425eed071718e4 tests where completion increases with weaker solvent and how that increase depends on amount.

m72 at 5/1, 50 ul in PE/300 ul can be compared with measured DCM/200 ul row 10f01f359bc6067d009f. Both loading-solvent identity and volume change, so this is a combined setup contrast. Existing high-loading PE coverage also makes it informative about setup-by-amount transfer beyond m168.

This additional m56 catalog row repeats 100/1, 50 ul conditions where 81cd2078a0008c2c9cd9 recorded completion at 7.85 mL. Higher-amount rows e7c4d856d4d9a8d5ddbf and 3016ab4b83227fcf83e4 finish near 25–27 mL, while the current low-amount forecast is 19.36 mL. The label assesses whether the short low-loading result is representative and informs the conditional prediction under recorded-feature variability.

m58 at 2/1, 50 ul forecasts onset later than measured 5/1 row 60c07f57327c89c83ae9 and even 10/1 row aafc5710406e440a4c8f. This starts an amount pair testing an unverified strong-solvent onset peak for a sterically substituted phenol, extending the question beyond the m208 and m209 environments.

m58 at 2/1, 150 ul completes the pair. Its forecast shifts onset earlier with amount but leaves completion almost unchanged. The two labels distinguish a real amount-dependent peak from an inappropriate alcohol or phenol response transferred into this sparsely measured region.

m38 at 5/1, 100 ul supplies the fixed-loading companion to selected 10/1. Recent high-loading rows 5b1b0390c90ceb580c5e and d1e922c04dbd0c9f6c06 show a substantial completion rise across these ratios. Measuring the same segment at the middle amount separates solvent slope from the emerging completion association with amount.

hypotheses.content: Amount associations depend on scaffold, PE/EA, and endpoint. Recent m208 and m67 contrasts support appreciable onset movement with comparatively stable completion, whereas m174 and m38 show that completion can also depend on amount. The supplied observations do not support a universal loading direction or a common endpoint correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing ratio segments and amount interpolations can teach separate V1 and V2 interactions across recurring chemical environments. Current forecasts already contain amount slopes, so the next labels test their adequacy and boundaries rather than simply challenging invariance.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1 does m174 completion change appreciably between middle and high amount, and do m35, m38, and m19 follow the current endpoint-specific amount responses in their missing solvent segments?

hypotheses.content: For m33, the completion association with amount changes with PE/EA. Higher loading finishes later in measured neat EA, 10/1, and 50/1 contrasts, while the measured 1/1 low-to-high contrast goes in the opposite direction. The response at 5/1, including possible nonlinear amount dependence, remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This scaffold provides direct evidence against a single completion-versus-amount adjustment. The missing 5/1 pair tests whether the retrained predictor captures a transition between neighboring recorded response patterns.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, what direction and magnitude of completion change occurs between 100 and 150 ul, and is the forecast near-flat response supported?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading-solvent identity and volume can carry predictive information beyond sample amount. Four measured m168 volume contrasts associate 400 ul DCM with earlier completion than 300 ul, including the latest contrast at a different sample amount. The m92 identity contrast is larger. Causality, reproducibility, and transfer across scaffolds remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A missing m168 counterpart and cross-scaffold setup comparisons test whether recorded loading information is underused and where a common adjustment would fail. The m72 comparison changes both identity and volume and will be interpreted as a joint setup association.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m168 volume association persist at 10/1 and 150 ul sample volume, and do m88 and m72 require distinct loading-setup mappings?

hypotheses.content: The m205 and m206 scaffold-plus-loading setups have different solvent responses despite similar calculated LogP and one OH group each. The latest low-loading labels establish a difference already at 1/1, before the larger 2/1 and 5/1 differences. Their different DCM loading volumes and densities prevent attribution solely to molecular structure.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The labels constrain how OH environment and recorded loading conditions jointly affect solvent curvature. They provide a direct test of whether the low-loading setup difference transfers across amount.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the high-loading 1/1 labels preserve the setup difference, and where does the m206 low-loading curve rise between its measured 1/1 and 5/1 endpoints?

hypotheses.content: m197-specific extended completion in strong solvent is supported across the measured neat-EA amount series; the forecast middle-amount trough was rejected. This does not justify transferring its response shape to all phenolic aldehydes. The forecast m190 strong-solvent peak and m186 intermediate onset hump remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Completion and onset need scaffold- and condition-specific curves. Testing the missing segments can distinguish supported extended intervals from unsupported interpolation peaks without imposing a global completion shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m197 completion rise at 10/1, and do the selected m190 and m186 conditions reproduce their forecast local peaks?

hypotheses.content: Some nonmonotone endpoint responses are present in the observations, while other forecast peaks and dips lack measured support. For example, m81 high-loading completion decreases from 5/1 to 10/1, but the m127 and m58 stronger-solvent onset peaks and the m75 weak-solvent completion dip are unverified. These cases require local discrimination rather than a blanket monotonicity correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Fixed-amount solvent segments and local amount contrasts can separate recorded exceptions from erroneous transfer. These labels may improve response surfaces across related carbonyl and OH environments without erasing genuine dataset variation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m81 completion decrease extend to middle loading, and are the forecast m127, m58, and m75 extrema supported when their missing conditions are measured?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen conditional loading reasoning while changing where further measurements are most useful. At 10/1, m208 onset moved from 16.52 to 12.96 mL between low and high amount while completion stayed near 27 mL. The m67 2/1 pair also retained onset movement, but its measured completions near 11 mL contradicted the acquisition forecasts near 17.65 mL. Current predictions have changed, so those historical errors are not treated as current residuals. For m33, the new 10/1 pair and neat-EA low-loading label support completion increases with amount at those ratios; the opposite measured 1/1 contrast makes the missing 5/1 segment especially informative. The m197 middle-amount neat-EA completion of 26.73 mL rejects its forecast trough and shifts attention to the missing weaker-solvent curve. The m205/m206 difference is now observed already at 1/1, supporting a high-loading comparison while preserving their setup confounding. The m168 high-amount volume pair repeated the modest completion association, motivating one missing counterpart and transfer tests instead of another full local volume pair. The m88 middle and high neat-EA completions are almost equal, weakening a middle-only peak interpretation. The m174 100/1 middle and high amounts both finished much later than forecast at acquisition, and m38 high-loading 10/1 completion was also underpredicted; the batch therefore targets their missing ratio and amount segments. The retired m84 short-interval transfer hypothesis receives no allocation, and the m73 endpoint inconsistencies remain recording issues rather than retention mechanisms.
batch_rationale: The batch uses controlled local experiments where each added label has a clear comparison. The m174, m35, m38, m19, and m33 conditions address different ways that amount and PE/EA can affect V1 and V2. The m205/m206 comparison and m208 segment extend recently supported solvent-response findings. One m168 complement, an m88 volume comparison, and an m72 combined loading-setup contrast test transfer of recorded loading information beyond a single scaffold. Exploration concentrates on specific unsupported curve shapes in m127, m58, m75, m190, and m186, while the m81 pair checks whether an observed nonmonotone completion response extends across amount. The m197 pair follows up a rejected interpolation shape by locating a missing solvent-response segment. One additional m56 row assesses whether a consequential short-completion observation is representative at its recorded conditions. This mix can improve structure-condition-endpoint mappings across recurring Row-distribution chemistry without requiring a common retention shift. Single-predictor quantile widths are secondary evidence and are not assumed calibrated epistemic uncertainty; elution interval widths describe chromatographic endpoints. All choices are frozen together before any new labels are revealed.
